# The implementer stages everything. A step that forbids bulk staging records the hit as the output violations, and the step still succeeds.
# The next step reads the output. A step that forbids another kind records nothing.
exec obee run 7 --workflow flow/hit.star
stdout 'item 7 finished'

grep -count=1 '^implement ' calls.log
grep -count=1 '^audit ' calls.log
grep -count=1 '^bulk-staging: git add -A$' seen.log

exec obee run 8 --workflow flow/miss.star
stdout 'item 8 finished'

grep -count=2 '^audit ' calls.log
grep -count=1 'git add' seen.log

# The fake claude now obeys --settings and runs the hook before the Bash call, as Claude Code does. The hook is `obee check command`.
# It exits 2 on the bulk staging, so the call is blocked and never ran: the output violations stay empty.
cp flow/hit.star obey-hook
exec obee run 9 --workflow flow/hit.star
stdout 'item 9 finished'

grep -count=1 '^blocked git add -A$' blocked.log
grep -count=3 '^audit ' calls.log
grep -count=1 'git add' seen.log

-- flow/hit.star --
def main(item):
    implement = agent(name = "implement", prompt = "prompts/implement.md", model = "sonnet", forbid_commands = ["bulk-staging", "local-delete"])
    agent(name = "audit", prompt = "prompts/audit.md", model = "sonnet", inputs = {"seen": implement.violations})
-- flow/miss.star --
def main(item):
    implement = agent(name = "implement", prompt = "prompts/implement.md", model = "sonnet", forbid_commands = ["remote-delete"])
    agent(name = "audit", prompt = "prompts/audit.md", model = "sonnet", inputs = {"seen": implement.violations})
